hook_text: A Scottish gardener, a desert spring, and the first complete Bible printed in an African language in southern Africa.
clip_script: Robert Moffat had little schooling and a gardener's hands. In 1824 he chose a spot in the dry Northern Cape beside the Kuruman Eye, a spring that never stops flowing. He dug furrows, and gardens bloomed. He built a stone church that still stands. With Tswana speakers teaching him their language, he wrote Setswana down and translated the whole Bible, printing it on his own press by 1857. He befriended kings like Mzilikazi. His work spread reading and writing, but also changed Tswana life in ways historians still debate.
visual_style: Clear water bubbling from a spring among reeds; an irrigation furrow leading to green gardens; a stone church; an old printing press stamping a Setswana page.
pacing: Gentle storytelling with a thoughtful final note.
